If you have never experienced Kingfish fishing, winter is the perfect time to visit a tropical saltwater destination to try your luck at catching a few. The Florida Keys is one of the best places to go fishing for Kingfish on the flats during the winter months.

Don't dismiss this less popular species just because it has a habit of lunging at other catches that you might be reeling in. Make no mistake about it; the Kingfish's hard runs and spectacular jumps are sure to get your heart pounding with excitement.

If you're not sure where to look or what type of Kingfish fishing equipment you might need, these five tips can help.

You can find Kingfish on the saltwater flats, in channels, and near inshore structure. When other inshore game fish start acting fickle due to changes in the weather, Kingfish fishing on the flats can still be quite productive. Kingfish tend to school up in the shallows during cooler weather, making them prime sight casting targets. As water temperatures warm up on the flats with the arrival of spring, Kingfish will usually start moving off into deeper waters.

When fishing for Kingfish, you can use a 6½-foot medium-action Baitcasting reel and a 4000-series spinning reel spooled with 18-pound braided line. Distance casting is important to avoid spooking this fish species. Once a Kingfish spots you or your boat, it usually means the game is over.

Always use a wire leader on a Kingfish rig. Kingfish have razor-sharp teeth, which means you need to use wire leader that's light enough to go undetected, but strong enough to hold up against a Kingfish's toothy grin. When fishing for Kingfish with lures, use a fast retrieve. The best Kingfish lures give the appearance of prey fleeing through the water, but it's the combination of lure speed and appearance that will trigger a strike. You can try a brightly colored Kingfish tube lure or a silver swimming plug.

Last, but certainly not least, use caution and a good pair of heavy-duty pliers to remove hooks. If you plan to hold a Kingfish for a photo, hold the fish very firmly behind the head.

Use these helpful Kingfish fishing tips and get ready to catch your very first Kingfish. Before you go, just be sure to learn about the best times to saltwater fish so that you can plan your trip accordingly.
